pr_title: Fix exiting editor potentially causing a crash
pr_body:
There were a few weird cases with dialog display logic, so I did a complete pass on it. Hopefully it feels more robust now.

Note that I was not able to reproduce the exact scenario the user in the linked issue hit, even when adding delays in every potential asynchronous load location I could find. Regardless, my theory is that two calls to `Editor.Exit()` were happening, with the second fire hitting the early `confirmExit()` case:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/87833bfb6186ad9789c0eacf641471ed4739ab7e/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/Editor.cs#L479

This has been resolved with the changes I've made (to use button press flow instead). I've also standardised how this is done as much as possible between the main menu and editor, as they have very similar flows.

Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/12859.
pr_comments: In combining the exit logic, I broke some tests. I think the fix applied makes sense, but worth taking a close look at the last commit to make sure you agree with this direction.

On a pure black-box test level, I could reproduce the exact issue as the reporter, and this PR seems to fix it. The behaviour I was seeing is that on `master`, you could exit editor, but then the dialog overlay would exit after a significant delay, when already out in the main menu. On this branch, however, whatever causes the overlay delay also blocks exit from the editor screen, fixing the issue as presumably no leases have been returned yet.

Going to look at the code now, but unsure if I'm going to be able to dig up the exact root cause in the time I've got left today.

This has spiraled a bit out of control, but likely improved code quality at the same time.

The new commits should stand alone as to what their intent is, but request if you'd prefer I split them out into their own PR.

Actually I will definitely consider splitting the changes out, but before I do so @bdach can you have a quick check and see if you agree with the direction?

There's a couple of tests which are still failing due to reference comparisons of `BeatmapInfo` which now fail due to an internal re-fetch (where `Files.Count` is 0, which never used to trigger a fetch) but I won't fix those until I get another opinion as to whether this is a good/correct direction.

This whole logic is very flaky and really shouldn't be, considering how central it is to the whole game.

On a turbo quick look I have no big issues with the latest commits. One thing I'm not 100% is the ordering changes in `GetWorkingBeatmap()` (why requery before checking `previous` if it's going to possibly get returned anyway?) but other than that, doesn't look too wrong.

Can't look more properly right now, sorry. Still need a few more hours until I can be able to shift focus fully here.

The ordering issue you mention is likely just an oversight (I didn't read that specific line in context of the surrounding ones).

Also no worries. I don't think there's a huge hurry to fix this one so take your time (even though it's priority 0, it's pretty rare to actually encounter it in normal usage).

I've read the last few commits again in a more leisurely manner, and it took me the better part of an hour to retrace what exactly tripped this. To make sure we're on the same page, as far as I understand, the trail of breadcrumbs goes as follows:

1. `ScreenTestScene` (which `EditorTestScene` derives from) adds an exit screen step at the start of each test.
2. This trips the `BeatmapManager` refetch logic in `Editor.OnExiting()`.
3. Because `TestBeatmap` was specifying an empty list of `Files` and not `null`, the null-checked refetch here:

    https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/7845d07dd53d2a282a7bf1c20245b22edb718801/osu.Game/Beatmaps/BeatmapManager.cs#L293-L297

    does not fire, and is instead incorrectly interpreted as a proper beatmap despite having no beatmap data.
4. Even after fixing up `Files` to not trip up on nullability, `BeatmapManager` can return a `DummyWorkingBeatmap` on that same check (if the map doesn't yet exist in DB), which discards everything that `TestBeatmap` had set up previously and breaks tests, which is where the proposed addition of a test `BeatmapManager` comes in, as it ensures this cannot happen, and the same `WorkingBeatmap` is always returned from `GetWorkingBeatmap()`.

If I have the above right, then I definitely agree with splitting this off to a separate PR, and the general proposed direction seems fine - I can't see how to otherwise work out those two kinks. There are still: the check reordering issue pointed out above, the failing CI checks (some unresolved inspections) and some straggler test failures you mentioned, but once that is resolved I don't think I would have any objections.

Yep, that's the exact sequence of unfortunate events that took a quick fix to a several hour long descent into wondering if we are doing everything completely wrong 😅.

I'll take another look at this later today and either come up with a miraculous alternative or a cleaned up PR for the changes. A bit unsure about making `Files` non-nullable as it triggers part of the issue, but does seem like the correct path forward? With the next step potentially being to do that for all `IHasFiles` implementations.

Yeah I'd say so. My immediate thought is that null file list and empty file list should really both mean the same thing, which is "there are no files", so it is definitely the correct thing to have one "empty" value to check against and not two. And if there *is* a place that relies on this distinction in some capacity, then that damn well needs to be fixed, too.

issue_context.title: Able to exit the editor before the confirmation dialog appears, potentially crashing the game
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** 
1. Open the game
2. Enter the editor as quick as possible and spam <kbd>Esc</kbd> to exit
3. The main menu appears first, then the confirmation dialog appears a few moments later.

At this stage, clicking "Forget all changes" causes the game to crash with the exception:

review_comments:
I'm not sure I get what's happening here. From what I can gather this and the `StartHidden` specification are two parts of a particular setup, but I'm not sure what this setup is supposed to achieve. If I understand correctly:

* `VisibilityContainer`s already start hidden by default
* `StartHidden` makes super absolutely sure that they start hidden by default and don't play any animations to boot by finishing transforms, but also doesn't change `State`

so this is basically a workaround to have `State` be `Visible` in ctor, then have `VisibilityContainer.LoadAsyncComplete()` play the pop-out instantly but keep the `Visible` state, and then finally `LoadComplete()` run `UpdateState()` and therefore also run the pop-in animation? And with this setup any changes in the ctor-to-`LoadComplete()` time interval can be detected while they would be previously lost?

If the above is right, then even though the end goal I can agree with, I'm not entirely sure how to feel about the path there. Feels like a rube goldberg type solution if I'm honest.

`StartHidden` is strictly animation related. It makes the "pop in" animation play on first display, rather than immediately showing the shown state.

But yes, in practice it's doing exactly what you mention.

I think most of my confusion is in that visibility container members are just confusingly named - enabling `StartHidden` feels like it should also mutate `State`, but it doesn't.

That's not in scope here, though, so I guess I could personally live with it at the end of the day - would maybe leave a comment at that `StartHidden` override that it's related to the show call, since it might not be as obvious N months down the line...
